messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: gpu-hotpath-saturation in eu-west-1 (threshold breached: gpu-pool hotpath util > 95%). Priority: P1. Runbook: /runbooks/gpu-saturation. Paging oncall-neo and eng-sre.
maya: seeing a lot of 429s in frontend logs, customers reporting failures. stack traces show tokenbucket rejects. example: `{"status":429,"reason":"token_bucket_exhausted","pool":"hotpath-gpu-1"}`
oncall-neo: I'm on call. digging in now. any immediate mitigation suggestions? can we temporarily route some traffic to dedicated-coldpool?
raj: confirm hotpath queue depth spiked ~18k requests over the last 3m. autoscaler didn't pick up because the tokenwindow lock prevented pool backfill. suspect tokenbucket refill rate + tiered-policy mismatch.
dana: timeline: ~15:03 CPU/gpu autoscale heartbeats delayed, then large enqueue at 15:05. ratepolicy log shows `tier: hot -> tokenbucket refilled 0` (looks like a mis-evaluated policy that zeroed refill for hot tier).
liam: grabbing k8s node metrics now. `kubectl get pods -n inference hotpath-gpu-1 -o wide` shows pods in CrashLoopBackOff for some infer-sidecar threads. but main issue is throttling earlier than capacity exhaustion.
emily: customers A and B on dedicated tiers reported 429s and latency spikes. support queue has ~12 open tickets referencing `429`. tagging account managers.
maya: can we raise token refill for hotpath temporarily? also maybe increase per-connection burst for the tier. worried about cascading cost though.
oncall-neo: trying conservative change first: bump tokenbucket refill for pool hotpath-gpu-1 to 3x for 10m. executing CLI:

```
# ephemeral change
rictl ratepolicy set --pool hotpath-gpu-1 --token-refill 300 --token-cap 1200 --reason "ephemeral mitigation 3x refill"
```
ops-bot: ratepolicy change accepted (request id rpo-2026-0315-001). Policy propagation to edge proxies starting.
raj: logs showing immediate drop in 429s for certain routes but still seeing tail 429s because tier mapping unmatched: hot requests routed to tier=standard due to header mismatch.
dana: patching routing rule now to ensure header X-Redwood-Tier is honored for hotpool traffic:
```
# update edge rule
edgectl set-route --match-path /v1/hot/* --set-header X-Redwood-Tier=hot
```
liam: after route patch, 429s dropped by ~65% in the last 90s, queue length decaying. autoscaler still slow to fill because of a tokenwindow lock; working a restart of the autoscaler leader elector.
oncall-neo: restarting autoscaler leader on eu-west-1 (rolling) — should not disrupt existing pools. `kubectl rollout restart deploy/autoscaler -n infra` in progress.
ops-bot: deploy/autoscaler restarted, new leader elected.
maya: observed additional capacity pop in over the last 2 min, hotpool pod count +6. queue now decreasing steadily.
emily: notifying CS teams and affected customers: sending templated update: "We observed a transient throttling issue causing 429s; mitigation underway. Will follow up with RCA." (posted)
raj: note for postmortem: root cause likely combination of (1) a ratepolicy regression that set refill=0 for hot tier under certain conditions, (2) route header mismatch that made some hot traffic look standard, and (3) autoscaler leader delay due to long GC pause.
dana: recording immediate action items: roll back the bad ratepolicy commit, add unit tests for tier-eval, ensure route header precedence in edge rules, and add a guard to prevent token-refill=0 on hot tiers.
liam: suggested medium-term: add a circuit to bypass tokenbucket for emergency critical customers (configurable), and an autoscaler override API for oncall to force pool backfill.
oncall-neo: current status: 429s largely mitigated, queue < 800 and trending down, hotpool stable at 12 pods, no new customer escalations in last 10m. handing off to maya for follow-up and RCA. I'm dropping off at 16:00Z PST.
maya: taking handoff. I'll open an incident postmortem doc and link the commits and logs. immediate bridge notes saved to /incidents/3041592653.
ops-bot: reminder: create follow-up ticket: ENG-IR-3041592653 (auto-created) assigned to eng-sre with priority P2 for RCA and policy fixes.
emily: adding notes to customer comms tracker and scheduling a postmortem sync with CS and product tomorrow 1400 UTC.
maya: thanks all — great quick mitigation. action owners: raj (root-cause triage), dana (ratepolicy revert + tests), liam (autoscaler leader GC hardening), emily (customer comms). closing oncall handoff thread. :white_check_mark:
